3 03-02-2026 1-Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor representing the State.

2-This appeal under Sections 415 (2) and 430 (1) of the B.N.S.S. has been preferred by the appellant namely Md Asfaque Hussain @ Asfaque Hussain against the judgment of conviction dated 26.05.2025 and order of sentence dated 02.06.2025 passed by the learned Sessions Judge,
Kishanganj in Sessions Trial (S.T) No. 32 of 2020 arising out of Pothia P.S. Case No. 203 of 2019 under Sections 341, 323, 307, 326, 504, 506 and 498-A/34 of the Indian Penal Code District Kishanganj, convicting and sentencing the appellant as under:-
(a) 10 years' rigorous imprisonment for the offence Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ)
No.3004 of 2025(3) dt.03-02-2026 under Section 304B of the IPC.

(b) 3 years' rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.
10,000/- for the offence under Section 498A of the IPC and in default of payment of fine, 3 months'
additional simple imprisonment.
All the sentences are ordered to run concurrently.
3-The appellant has prayed for suspension of his sentence and release on bail during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal before this Court.

sentences.text: 4-Brief facts of the case, which are required to be stated are that it is alleged by the prosecution inter-alia that niece of the informant namely Bebi was married to accused Asfaque Hussain as per Muslim rites and customs and customary gifts were voluntarily given at the time of marriage.
Initially, the marriage remained cordial and a child was born from the wedlock.

Subsequently, it is alleged that accused Asfaque Hussain and other named accused persons started assaulting her on trivial issues and subjected her to cruelty for demand of dowry of Rs. 1 lakh, ornaments and a cow from her parental home.
It is further alleged that on 19.11.2019, the accused persons assaulted the deceased and threatened her to oust her from the matrimonial home.

On receiving this information,
the Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3004 of 2025(3) dt.03-02-2026 informant went to her matrimonial house to pacify the matter.

On 20.11.2019 at about 3:00 p.m., the accused persons,
including Asfaque Hussain, allegedly assaulted Bebi, poured kerosene oil on her, and attempted to set her on fire, causing severe burn injuries over a major portion of her body.
Upon learning of the incident, the informant, with the help of villagers, took her to Pothia Hospital, from where she was referred for further treatment.
5-It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
Impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence of the appellant is not sustainable in the eyes of the law.
Appellant is the husband of the deceased.

Apart from merit of the case much emphasis has been given by contending that the maximum sentence awarded to the appellant is up to 10 years and he is in jail since 23.06.2020 as such, till date, appellant has served incarceration of 5 years 7 months and 11 days therefore, considering the detention period of the appellant he may be released on bail.
Lastly, it is submitted that on account of huge pendency of cases before this Court, there is no likelihood of the appeal being heard in near future.
In case appellant is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.3004 of 2025(3) dt.03-02-2026 early hearing of this appeal.

6-Learned A.P.P. for the State though opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant by contending that the prosecution has proved it's case beyond reasonable doubts, hence at this stage presumption of innocence is not available to the appellant.
7-Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as looking to the long detention period of the appellant in jail as mentioned above,
I find that he has made out a case for grant of bail in the light of judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Saudan Singh vs. State of U.P., 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3259, wherein, it has been observed by the Apex Court that there may be even convicts in custody in cases other than life sentence cases and in those cases again the broad parameter of 50 percent of the actual sentence undergone can be the basis for grant of bail and in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. C.B.I, (2022) 10 SCC 51 wherein, it has been observed inter- alia that when a person has undergone detention for a period extending to one- half of the maximum period of imprisonment specified for that offence, he shall be released by the court on his personal bond with or without sureties.

sentences.text: "Before parting with order, we must note here that notwithstanding several decisions of this Court holding that when there is a fixed term sentence and especially when the appeal is not likely to be heard before completing entire period of sentence, normally suspension of sentence and bail should be granted. We find that in several deserving cases, bail is being denied.
Such cases should never be required to be brought before this Court".
9-Hence, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, the sentence of the appellant is suspended during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal.

10-Let the appellant- Md Asfaque Hussain @ Asfaque Hussain be enlarged on bail during pendency of this appeal in above Case on his furnishing bail bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned subject to deposit of 50% amount fine.
The realization of remaining 50% amount of fine shall remain stayed till disposal of this Criminal Appeal.

11-On acceptance of the bail bonds, the concerned Court Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3004 of 2025(3) dt.03-02-2026 below shall furnish the photocopy thereof to this Court for being kept on record of this Criminal Appeal.
12-Let this Criminal Appeal be listed in due course for hearing.

(Sanjay Kumar Singh , J) Prakash/-
